t: Find the Sequence of Strings Appeared on the Screen
o: Alice types target using 'append a' and 'increment last char'. The minimum-press sequence is forced: for each target character, press key 1 (screen grows by 'a'), then press key 2 until the last character equals the target character. We must output every intermediate screen contents. With |target| ≤ 400 each character costs at most 26 presses, so at most ~10,400 strings — simulation is trivially fast.
k: The optimal typing is deterministic: append 'a', then increment the last letter to the target character; there is no cheaper route to each prefix.
Every intermediate string must be emitted, so the output size itself is O(26·n) and dominates the runtime.
